analysis.title: BINARIES 8 Oct 2026
key_insights: Oil and refining cracks are higher on a pickup in Iran attacks and the market's growing expectation that Trump resumes bombing. Rates rose initially overnight, then USTs twist-flattened. US equities still do not 'hold the L' because AI megacap tech, which drives the index, is acting rates insensitive.

The winning trade YTD is 'Long the AI Core Constraints': long semis plus long energy (commodities), with an Iran-driven inflation shock and rate vol as a kicker. The pair is +65% YTD on a 3.2 Sharpe and carries a built-in rates hedge. Bonds have not worked as a long or as an equity hedge amid sticky inflation and energy-driven rate vol spasms.

Over about 2 months since early August, SPX has moved less than 1% in aggregate after July's momentum de-gross / AI unwind shock. Index vol metrics are near multi-year lows: 10-day realized vol 7, 1m 10, 2m 9.5.

SPX 3m ATM implied vol is at the 2nd percentile (1Y). SPX skew (25 delta put / 25 delta call) is at the 0.4th percentile over 1Y, and put skew is also 0.4th percentile. SPX 1DTE ATM straddle is at the 9th percentile (2Y).

High dispersion and low correlation are driven by a 'thematic bifurcation'. A small cluster of AI winners does the heavy lifting for the index, while everything else suffers from capital crowding-out, an enthusiasm vacuum, perceived AI disruption risk and, recently, 'rates loser' status.

Rate-sensitive sectors have already had a 'rolling correction'. Over the trailing 30 days only TMT and Energy are higher. Healthcare is -3.5%, Consumer Discretionary -3.6%, Utilities -4.6%, Industrials -5.8%, Financials -7.7%, Materials -7.9% and REITs -9.8%.
Breadth of drawdowns in the S&P 500: 85% of names are more than 10% below their all-time highs, 59% more than 20%, 41% more than 30%, 26% more than 40% and 17% more than 50%.

Index vol supply is massive, especially intraday in 0DTE/1DTE (looks like QIS VRP flows). It leaves dealers long gamma, which suppresses realized vol. Exotics and structured note flows are growing prolifically this year and add vega supply to dealers.
Low realized vol has let vol-scaling systematic strategies add exposure back. Vol Control + CTA + Risk Parity US equity exposure is back at the 86th percentile, near the year's highs.

Demand for downside hedges is weak and skew 'chokes' daily. SPX call skew is at the 99.6th percentile, showing extreme relative demand for OTM calls. Many institutions are under-invested in the narrow AI sleeve, and market-neutral hedge funds lack the net exposure to capture the low-breadth rally, which creates pressure to re-risk.

Investors tried to de-risk ahead of next week's earnings kickoff, citing macro/rates risk, midterms, the Anthropic IPO timing and AI capex financing supply (OpenAI seeking $50B for AVGO chips, ORCL/Apollo/GS chip financing, SPCX for NVDA chips). Improving earnings breadth, AI capex trickle-down and nominal GDP of 7-9% let corporates and equities absorb higher rates.

Energy is the fragile point: cracks equal rate vol. Europe and Asia are short energy and the world ex Asia/India is short refinery capacity. Emergency stock releases (pushed by Trump's diesel ban bluster) buy only a bit over a month of supply. McElligott believes Trump will resume Iran attacks regardless of the election result, and that refining capacity is the binding constraint whatever flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

Trade ideas: megacap tech call spreads into an equity rally over the next month, helped by 99th percentile call skew and a buyside underpositioned for SPX 8k. Iran deal talk into midterms would hit energy and rate vol, favoring Gold and IWM upside. Hedge with long USD/EUR rates vega via long-dated swaption straddles (Nomura QIS Irving swaps), since terminal rate expectations could reprice into restrictive territory even on strong earnings.

Energy is the second AI constraint (power/infra) and is higher over 30 days. It is the long-energy leg of the semis-energy barbell, supported by Iran-driven supply risk and refining shortages.
REITs fell 9.8% over the trailing 30 days, the worst sector, as a rates loser.
Financials fell 7.7% over 30 days in the rolling correction of rate-sensitive sectors.
